newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea threatens to give up contacts with U.S..
newsitem.headline: N.Korea threatens to give up contacts with U.S..

text.p: North Korea on Monday accused the United States of attempting to contain it militarily and threatened to stop dealing with Washington over a 1994 landmark nuclear agreement.

The warning came in a newspaper commentary on recent visits to Japan and South Korea by U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen and the Chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff General John Shalikashvili.
"The fact reveals their attempt to contain the DPRK (North Korea) militarily hand in glove with Japan and the South Korean puppets," the Rodong Sinmun newspaper said.
The newspaper commentary was carried by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) monitored in Tokyo.

"If the United States is really interested in the implementation of the agreed framework and the improvement of bilateral ties, it would be well advised to take practical steps favourable to removing distrust and building confidence between the two countries," the commentary said.

"If the United States does not try to take such steps beyond words in relations with the DPRK, we would not feel it necessary to continue dealing with the United States any longer but be left with no other choice than taking countermeasures," it said.

Under a $4.5 billion deal signed in 1994, Washington promised North Korea two light-water reactors in return for the isolationist state's pledge to freeze and ultimately dismantle its existing nuclear programme.
Light-water reactors are less suitable for producing weapons-grade plutonium than the graphite-moderated reactors built by North Korea.
"We have a right to take a choice and measures to take for the defence of the sovereignty, interests and security of the country," the North Korean commentary added.

"In case the United States persistently resorts to adventurous military threat to the DPRK with double-dealing tactics, we will increase the military strength and power and take a strong countermeasure," it said.
